title: Introduction to Financial Planning
description: Explores money management, and wealth creation strategies to include a personal financial plan. Stocks, Bonds, Mutual Funds, Real Estate, Money Markets, Insurance needs, transportation options, and retirement planning. Consumer Credit, Predatory Lending, Identity Theft are also covered.

title: Business Management Capstone
description: A practical application course directing students in the development of an updated Resume, Cover Letter and Skill-Based Career Portfolio demonstrating individual competency in Business Management Program Outcomes. This course should be completed in the spring of a student's final ATA year.
prerequisites: By permission of Instructor.

title: Introduction to International Business
description: This International Business course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the global business environment and the complexities of conducting business on an international scale. The course encompasses a broad range of topics, offering insights into the economic, cultural, legal, and managerial aspects of international business . By the end of the course, students will have a holistic understanding of international business concepts, enabling them to make informed decisions and contribute effectively in a globalized business environment. Formerly BMGMT 102

title: Business and Personal Mathematics
description: Solving practical business and personal financial situations in an applied context including the development, critique, and use of various financial models. Concepts covered include Banking, Credit, Loans, Wages, Taxes, Budgeting, Investments, Insurance, the Metric System, PV/FV Value, Discounting, Cost, and Markups. Formerly BMGMT 140 Prerequisite: MATH 091 with a grade of 2.0 or above or satisfactory placement test score.

title: Improving Human Effectiveness
description: Effective leaders and managers are clear on their strengths and how they can be used in personal/professional settings. Explores how strengths can create a fulfilling career and life. Formerly OLRM 150

title: Introduction to Human Resources
description: This course examines policies and practices used in managing Human Resources to build and maintain an effective workforce. Topics include planning, recruitment, retention, and the HR legal environment. Formerly BMGMT 155

title: Marketing
description: Marketing has changed from one-way messaging to a conversation between companies and their customers. This course not only explores consumer buying behavior, target markets and trends, but it will assist you in better understanding your customer, so you know how to motivate them to engage with your business. In this course you will learn a variety or marketing strategies and tactics to establish and maintain long-term relationships with your current and future customers. Completing ENGL& 101 prior to taking this course is highly recommended due to the amount of research and writing that will be required during the course. Formerly BMGMT 180 Prerequisite: ENGL& 101 recommended.

title: E-Business Strategies
description: E-Business Strategies is designed to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the dynamic world of electronic business. The course focuses on the strategic use of digital technologies to enhance business operations, improve competitiveness, and capitalize on opportunities in the online marketplace. Students will explore key concepts and strategies related to electronic business, covering topics such as e-commerce, digital marketing, online presence, and technology-enabled business models. The course emphasizes practical applications and strategic decision-making in the context of the rapidly evolving digital landscape. Formerly BMGMT 185
prerequisites: A Marketing course is highly recommended.

title: Intro to Leadership & Business Management
description: Introduction to leadership and management within organizations. An exploration of the history of leadership & management theories, case studies, and understanding the relationship between management, leadership, motivation, and power. Formerly OLRM 201 and BMGMT 282

title: Introduction to Organizational Ethics
description: Introduction to organizational ethics, understanding the correlation between leadership/ management practice and the reflectiveness of moral philosophy, applying ethical decision making to ethical dilemmas. Formerly OLRM 202

title: Small Business Planning & Management
description: The Small Business Planning and Management course is designed to provide students with the essential knowledge and skills necessary for successfully launching and managing a small business. This course can assist in determining the feasibility of a small business venture, identifying start-up costs, comparing legal forms of ownership, and integrating a marketing strategy to meet business goals.
prerequisites: Completion of ENGL, ACCT and Marketing coursework recommended.

title: Systems Thinking for Leaders
description: Exploring how leaders impact and/or change organizations by understanding the patterns and relationships at work within their organizations. Formerly OLRM 218 Prerequisite: LBM 201 .

title: Human Relations in Organizations
description: (DSJ) This course is a "total person" approach to human relations. The focus is on the seven major themes of effective human relations: Communication, Self-Awareness, Self-Acceptance, Motivation, Trust, Self-Disclosure, and Conflict Resolution. An emphasis is placed on contributing to an inclusive workplace. Formerly OLRM 225

title: Conflict Resolution
description: Introduces students to the fundamentals of conflict resolution. Provides the knowledge and skills necessary to manage conflict, encourage cooperation, and create resolutions. Students will apply conflict identification, prevention, and resolution strategies to case studies in conflict resolution. Through reading, writing, and class participation; students will gain theoretical and practical knowledge for navigating personal and professional conflict. Formerly OLRM 260

title: Capstone Project
description: A practical application of theories, practices and concepts studied within the LBM program. This practical application can come through an internship, immersion program, a project within the workplace or other methods of experiential learning as agreed upon by student and instructor. Formerly BMGMT 299 and OLRM 299 Prerequisite: Successful completion of LBM 102 , LBM 202 , LBM 225 , and LBM 260 , or instructor permission.

title: Adaptive Keyboarding-One-Handed
description: Students will learn and develop skill in alphanumeric keyboarding and 20-key data entry using a one-handed keyboard.

title: Screen Magnification
description: Students will acquire the skills and knowledge to access and manipulate text using screen magnification.

title: Braille Translation and Printing
description: Comprehensive introduction to translating an ink-print document into Braille using a Braille translation program and printing in Braille. Prerequisite: BSTEC 104 .

title: Screen Reader Software Level 1
description: Introduction to the basics of voice-output software in a Windows environment. Instruction and use of basic keyboard commands to access and hear text voiced on the computer screen. JAWS or other screen reader technology.
prerequisites: Keyboarding skills.

title: Screen Reader Software Level 2
description: Instruction on producing, reading, and manipulating a word processing document using PC curser commands to access menu bars and icons using JAWS or other screen reader technology. Prerequisite: BSTEC 104 .

title: Screen Reader Software Level 3
description: The use of voice output to access and read graphic-based, mouse-driven environments, such as Windows desktop and web pages. Prerequisite: BSTEC 105 .

title: Voice Recognition Level 1
description: Introduction to DragonDictate. Use basic voice-activated input commands to build voice files, dictate a simple written document, and correct errors.

title: Voice Recognition Level 2
description: Learn to format and manipulate a document using intermediate voice-activated commands. Prerequisite: BSTEC 107 .

title: Doc. Processing with Speech Tec.
description: Basic Document Processing with speech technologies: Dragon, Windows Speech, etc. Substitutes for BSTEC 111 , when BSTEC speed requirement not met.
prerequisites: Computer competency recommended.

title: Beginning Keyboarding
description: Learn and develop skill in alphanumeric keyboarding, 10-key data entry, basic computer functions, and basic document formatting. ,

title: Intermediate Keyboarding
description:
Improve speed and accuracy of alphabetical and numerical data entry including business document formatting and 10-key pad skills using the touch system. Prerequisite: BSTEC 110 or equivalent.
,

title: Internet Basics
description: Introduction to tools and strategies to communicate, explore, and retrieve information using the Internet resources. Some computer skills required. Text required.

title: MS Outlook
description: Introduction to MS Outlook as an information manager. E-mail, files, contact lists, journal and calendar. Basic computer skills needed. Text required.

title: Electronic Communication
description: Write effective E-mail, use instant messaging, understand confidentiality and legal aspects, and use professional English to write, edit, and proofread before hitting send.

title: MS Word
description: Introduction to word processing with Microsoft Word for simple applications. Hands-on training. Textbook required. (Pass/No Credit or graded option)

title: MS Excel
description: Introduction to spreadsheets using Microsoft Excel for simple applications. Hands-on training. Textbook required. (Pass/No Credit or graded option)

title: MS PowerPoint
description: Understanding presentation software using Microsoft PowerPoint for simple applications. Hands-on training. Textbook required. (Pass/No Credit or grade)

title: MS Access
description: Microsoft Access database system, file structures and practical applications in the Windows environment. Computer skills suggested. Text required.

title: MS Transitions
description: Transition Microsoft Office skills using illustrated approach to most significant changes in terminology, features, and platform (Word, Excel, Access and PowerPoint).

title: MS Word Specialist
description:
Specialist approach to MS Word. Topics: formatting, editing, tables, columns, mail merge, graphics, Web pages. Use Word in business and help prep for the MOS Cert. test. Prerequisite: CIS 150 and keyboarding by touch, or permission of instructor.
,

title: MS Excel Specialist
description:
Specialist approach to MS Excel: formulas, logical functions, charts, hyperlinks, graphics, formatting, and managing data. Use Excel in business and help prep for the MOS test. Prerequisite: CIS 150 or permission of instructor.
,

title: Intro to MS Office PowerPoint
description: Use MS Office PowerPoint to create and edit a presentation, augment with design, graphics, audio/video, and other formatting, and enhance slideshow techniques. ,

title: Integration of Software Applications
description: Reinforce understanding and proficiency with MS Office, completing tasks in Word, Excel, Access and PowerPoint, and integrating between these applications. Prerequisite: CIS 150 or permission of instructor.

title: Practical Accounting
description: Introductory accounting course that includes accounting theory and practice as they apply to small business and service business situations.

title: Electronic Printing Calculators
description: Control and operation of electronic printing and display calculators. Emphasis on attaining minimum Office proficiency. ,

title: Computerized Accounting
description:
Hands-on, realistic approach to computerized, integrated accounting for students who have a fundamental knowledge of accounting practices and principles. Prerequisite: BSTEC 130 or ACCT& 201 , or permission of instructor.
,

title: Payroll Accounting
description: Designed to provide information and study regarding the benefits, taxes, payroll deductions, and employment accounting records incidental to the social security and tax program.

title: Accounting Simulation/Service Business
description: Simulated accounting application involving the accounting cycle for a service business. Prerequisite: BSTEC 130 or ACCT& 201 .

title: Accounting Simulation/Merchandising Business
description: Simulated accounting application involving the accounting cycle for a merchandising business. Prerequisite: BSTEC 130 or ACCT& 201 .

title: Accounting Simulation/Corporation
description: Simulated accounting application involving the accounting cycle for a corporation. Prerequisite: ACCT& 202 .

title: Payroll Simulation
description: Simulate the payroll accounting process using computer software to apply various workplace scenarios, including converting manual procedures to automated systems. Prerequisite: BSTEC 134 .

title: QuickBooks
description:
A hands-on, realistic approach to small business accounting using specialized QuickBooks accounting software and integration with Microsoft Word and Excel. Prerequisite: BSTEC 130 or ACCT& 201 or permission of instructor.
,

title: Business Writing/Grammar for the Workplace
description: A workplace-centered approach to improving writing skills by reviewing grammar, language usage, and punctuation, and using effective composition to write and revise basic workplace/business documents, including memos, letters, and reports. Prerequisite: Appropriate placement score to enter ENGL 098 ; or 2. 5 grade or higher in ENGL 091 ; or instructor permission.

title: Business English
description: A business-centered approach to improving writing skills by reviewing grammar, language usage, structure, English mechanics, editing, proofreading, and spelling. Prerequisite: Assessment test at college level reading and writing or ENGL 099 OR BSTEC 145.

title: MS Access Specialist
description: Specialist approach to MS Access. Design and development of databases. The creation and use of tables, various types of queries, forms and macros. Formerly CIS 154
prerequisites: Skill with using Windows and Files is recommended.

title: Communication Skills for Customer Service
description: Students will demonstrate communication competency while maintaining quality customer service. Students will develop technology skills and use research tools common to a customer service environment to locate and provide appropriate information. Emphasis on digital/electronic communications, including telephone skills, Internet research, writing effective email and understanding confidentiality and legal aspects of customer service. Formerly BSTEC 155 - Customer Service in the Information Age

title: General Office Procedures
description:
Introduction to the Office environment, receptionist duties, equipment and supply control, bank services, payroll procedures, mail and resume/job hunting skills. Prerequisite: CIS 150 and BSTEC 110 or equivalent skills with permission of instructor.
,

title: Independent Study
description: Allows the student to pursue topics not offered in the College Catalog through in-depth coursework under the direction of an instructor. This course may include directed readings, coverage of special topics, and other independent study. The topic and scope of study, learning objectives, work required, methods of evaluation, and academic level (195 versus 295) will be determined in conference between the student and instructor. (can be offered in all subjects)
prerequisites: Instructor permission.

title: Business Computer Applications
description: Strategic use of software applications to support business activity with emphasis on tasks in business communications, accounting, business decision-making, and information management. Create professional documents, build effective business presentations, use problem-solving spreadsheet models and utilize database content to inform business decisions. Determine the appropriate software and integrate content to produce effective business projects.
prerequisites: Computer user familiar with the keyboard, browsing the internet, and common business software such as MS Office. Not a beginner level computer course. (Skills can be gained through personal use or formal coursework. ) This course meets a prerequisite for transfer to WWU's bachelor in business program.

title: Individual Taxation
description: Study of Federal Income taxation to develop basic understanding of tax preparation requirements for individuals.

title: Practical Fund Accounting
description: Accounting and reporting concepts, standards and procedures applicable to state and local governments, the federal government, and not-for-profit institutions. Prerequisite: ACCT& 201 and ACCT& 202 with a grade of 2.0 or higher.

title: Taxation for Business
description: Study of Federal Income taxation and Washington State business taxation and its application to business entities. Prerequisite: BSTEC 130 or ACCT& 201 .

title: Taxation Simulations
description: Simulate tax filings for both individual and business entities. Demonstrate knowledge of tax laws and required forms. Prerequisite: BSTEC 229 and BSTEC 239 .

title: Business Correspondence
description: Effective composition for business letters, memos, and reports. Includes writing style, tone, grammar, punctuation, and vocabulary. Prerequisite: BSTEC 150 , or permission of instructor; keyboarding ability.

title: Document Formatting
description: Develop industry-standard formatting and production skills with MS Word software by keying and formatting various forms of standard industry documents.
prerequisites: BSTEC 111, 123, proof of 30 NWAM keyboarding requirement, or instructor permission

title: Records and Database Management
description: A study of the principles and practices of records storage and retrieval using manual and automated database systems; includes ARMA rules and introduction to Access. Prerequisite: CIS 150 , keyboarding proficiency at 25 WAM, or permission of instructor.

title: Advanced Office Applications
description:
Integration of business-standard software skills focusing on MS Office Suite. Emphasis is on problem solving, collaboration, and independent thinking. Prerequisite: BSTEC 123 , BSTEC 124 , and BSTEC 255 or BSTEC 154 , keyboarding proficiency at 45 NWAM or permission of instructor.
,

title: Administrative Office Management
description: Designed for BSTEC or BMGMT students as capstone class, or for currently employed Office personnel desiring to expand their knowledge of administrative Office management. Prerequisite: BSTEC 160 or one year general Office support work experience.

title: Chemistry of the Environment
description:
Natural Science The basic principles of chemistry emphasizing how they apply to the Earth, its major components, and its ecosystems. Prerequisite: Completion of MATH 094 with a 2.0 or permission of the instructor.

title: Chemical Concepts w/Lab
description:
Natural Science Introduces chemical principles in nonmathematical format intended for the liberal arts student. Topics include food, energy, household chemicals, and drugs. Prerequisite: MATH 094 or permission of instructor.
,

title: Intro to Chemistry
description:
Natural Science Atomic structure, chemical bonding, quantitative chemical relationships, solutions, acids, bases, salts, buffers. An introduction to organic chemistry may be included. Primarily for ADN and Allied Health students. Prerequisite: MATH 099 or MATHI 099 with a 2.0 or above, or satisfactory placement test score.
,

title: Intro to Organic/Biochemistry
description:
Natural Science Organic compounds including nomenclature and reactions of: hydrocarbons, alcohols, aldehydes and ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amines. Biochemistry of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and enzymes, nucleic acids, metabolism. Prerequisite: Completion of CHEM& 121 with a 2.0 or better.
,

title: General Chemistry Prep
description: Natural Science Prepares students for CHEM& 141 by introducing problem-solving techniques, the metric system, measurements, atomic structure, stoichiometry, solution chemistry, bonding, and molecular shape. NOT transferable for credit for science or engineering students. Prerequisite: MATH 099 or MATHI 099 with a grade of 2.0 or above, or satisfactory placement test score.

title: General Chemistry I
description: Natural Science Principles of chemistry including stoichiometry, enthalpy, atomic theory, gasses, periodicity, chemical bonding. Prerequisite: CHEM& 139 or CHEM& 121 with a 2.0 or above or successful completion of chemistry exam, and MATH 099 or MATHI 099 with a 2.0 or above, or satisfactory placement test score.

title: General Chemistry II
description: Natural Science Principles of chemistry including organic chemistry, gasses, solid and liquid states, solutions, kinetics, equilibrium, thermodynamics, acids and bases. Prerequisite: CHEM& 141 with a grade of 2.0 or higher.

title: General Chemistry III
description: Natural Science Principles of chemistry relating to acid/base equilibrium systems, heterogeneous equilibrium systems, transition metal chemistry, electrochemistry and nuclear chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM& 142 with a grade of 2.0 or higher.

title: General Chemistry Lab I
description: Natural Science Principles of chemistry including organic chemistry, gases, solid and liquid states, solutions, kinetics, equilibrium, thermodynamics, acids and bases. Prerequisite: CHEM& 141 with a grade of 2.0 or higher or concurrent enrollment in CHEM& 141 .

title: General Chemistry Lab II
description: Natural Science Experiments illustrating general principles and quantitative relationships in chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM& 151 , CHEM& 142 with a 2.0 or higher or concurrent enrollment in CHEM& 142 .

title: General Chemistry Lab III
description: Natural Science Volumetric and Gravimetric experiments in quantitative analysis using computer acquisition and treatment of data. Qualitative analysis of solutions containing selected metallic ions and polyatomic anions using wet chemical methods as well as a computer simulation. Prerequisite: CHEM& 152 , CHEM& 143 with a grade of 2.0 or higher or concurrent enrollment in CHEM& 143 .

title: Organic Chemistry I
description: Natural Science An introduction to the alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes. Includes discussions of structure, including stereochemistry, chemical and physical properties, and substitution/elimination reactions. Prerequisite: CHEM& 142 with a grade of 2.0 or higher.

title: Organic Chemistry II
description: Natural Science Introduction to NMR, mass spectroscopy and free radical mechanisms. The structure, synthesis and reactions of alcohols, ethers, conjugated unsaturated systems, aromatics, aldehydes, and ketones. Prerequisite: CHEM& 241 with a grade of 2.0 or higher.

title: Organic Chemistry III
description: Natural Science Structure, nomenclature, synthesis and reactions of aldehydes and ketones, carboxylic acids and derivatives, B-dicarbonyl compounds, amines, aryl halides, carbohydrates, lipids, and amino acids/proteins. Prerequisite: CHEM& 242 .

title: Organic Chemistry Lab I
description: Natural Science Organic chemistry lab emphasizes mastery of techniques such as sample handling, filtration, measuring physical constants, recrystallization, extraction, GC, polarimetry, and refractometry. Prerequisite: CHEM& 241 or concurrent enrollment.

title: Organic Chemistry Lab II
description: Natural Science Organic chemistry lab emphasizes techniques such as simple, fractional, steam, and reduced pressure distillation; thin-layer, column, high-pressure liquid chromatography, and IR/ NMR spectroscopy. Prerequisite: CHEM& 251 , or CHEM& 242 or concurrent enrollment in CHEM& 251 .

title: Organic Chemistry Lab III
description: Natural Science Includes organic qualitative analysis, an oral presentation on a journal article, and an independent synthesis project. Prerequisite: CHEM& 252 , CHEM& 243 , or concurrent enrollment in CHEM& 243 .

prerequisites: None.

description: (H/DSJ) The goal of popular communication studies is to investigate how popular culture artifacts reflect a lived cultural experience, and how lived experience is influenced by popular culture. The study of popular communication is rooted in studies of folklore, rhetoric, storytelling, media, and the culture industry. description: (H/DSJ) The purpose of this course is to help students understand and engage in dialogue, performance, and theory regarding sex and gender in communication. Sex and Gender in Communication centers on the role of gender and sexuality as communication practice in our everyday lives. This course is designed to increase students' awareness of and sensitivity to other gender stereotypes, gendered biases, gendered communication practices, and the social, political, cultural, and historical contexts in which they live and communicate. This course will teach students to communicate effectively between and across multiple gender and sexuality divides as we reach out to diverse individuals and diverse audiences. Included are an introduction to major gender communication theories and principles, feminist and queer theory approaches to communication studies, and the application of these principles in local and global contexts. title: Introduction to Personal Computers
description: Introduction to personal computers for first time users. Computer terminology, PC hardware options, windows operating systems, basic software techniques and basic Internet use.

title: Information Systems Concepts
description: Explore the fundamentals of information processing. Topics include: hardware, software, networking, the Internet, programming, and databases.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Microsoft Windows XP or later. Competent keyboard skills.

title: Introduction to Operating Systems
description: An technical introduction to operating system theory and common operating systems found in business environments, like Windows and Linux, with hands-on activities. Prerequisite: CIS 110 or concurrent enrollment or permission of instructor. ,

title: Introduction to HTML

prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Microsoft Windows 95 or later. Competent keyboarding skills.

title: Intro to MS Visio
description: Introduction to Microsoft Visio to create flow diagrams, basic organizational charts, and network diagrams. Knowledge of basic computer skills suggested. Text required.

title: Logic and Pattern Matching

Formerly CIS 202 Prerequisite: MATH 091 within the last 6 years with a grade of 2.0 or above or satisfactory placement test score.

title: Exploring Coding
description: An exploration of computer programming for non-programmers presented in a fun, engaging, and visual format. ,

title: Programming Concepts
description: An introduction to programming concepts.

An introduction to applications development for Windows and the Web using Java applications and applets. Prerequisite: CIS 141 with a grade of 2.0 or above, or permission of instructor.
,

title: Java II Fundamentals of OOP
description:
Develops fundamental concepts and techniques for analysis, design, and implementation of computer programs using an object-oriented language. Includes graphical user interfaces, event-driven programming, recursive techniques, and data structures. Prerequisite: CIS 142 with a grade of 2.0 or above, or permission of instructor.
,

title: Introduction to C Language
description:
Writing C programs utilizing programming concepts obtained from CIS 141 . Introducing C syntax for program control, functions, arrays, pointers, and string manipulation. Prerequisite: CIS 141 with a grade of 2.0 or above, or permission of instructor.
,

title: Survey of Computing
description: Learn basic concepts of word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, email management, and the Internet. Students without sufficient prior computer skills might benefit from taking CIS 100 first. To self-assess, please take this survey: https://bit.ly/cis-placement-survey ,

title: Web Development I
description:
Students are introduced to HTML5 elements and CSS3 to develop simple Web pages that integrate responsive (mobile) design, media, tables, and forms to produce consistent, navigable Web sites. Prerequisite: CIS 110 or concurrent enrollment, or instructor permission
,

title: Multimedia for the Web
description: Students will explore how digital multimedia is optimized to integrate into a HTML5 web page based on current standards and technologies. Managing and manipulating fonts, images, audio, video, and animation formats and codecs, and issues with hosting and legal considerations will also be covered.
prerequisites: None, though proficiency with HTML is helpful.

title: Technical Support Skills
description: Fundamentals of PC hardware and peripherals, mobile device hardware, networking and troubleshooting hardware and network connectivity issues. Installing and configuring operating systems including Windows, iOS, Android, Apple OS X and Linux. Also introduces security, the fundamentals of cloud computing and operational procedures. This course helps prepare students for the CompTIA A + 220-1001 and 220-1002 exams. Both exams are required for CompTIA A + certification. ,

title: Networking Concepts
description: This course is designed to introduce LAN/WAN terminology, design, topologies, protocols, various network hardware components, the TCP/IP network protocol, software, cabling and connectivity.

title: Information System Project Management
description: The student will learn, apply, analyze and evaluate significant information technology projects from initiation through closing. ,

title: SQL
description: Introduction to structured query language (SQL) used by most relational databases. Students will create, manipulate, and query data using DDL and DML. This class is intended for students with fundamental skills in computer programming. Students are strongly encouraged to contact faculty before enrolling in this class to review the prerequisite skills and knowledge needed for a successful experience. The prerequisite skills may be obtained by taking CIS 141 . ,

title: Windows for Professionals
description: Students will learn how to deploy, configure, secure, manage, and monitor device and client applications in a Microsoft enterprise environment. Skills covered include: deploying, maintaining, and updating Windows; configuring connectivity; managing policies and profiles; managing and protecting devices; and managing applications and data. This course helps prepare students for the MD-100 Windows 10 and MD-101 Management Modern Desktops exams to achieve their Microsoft 365 Certified: Modern Desktop Administrator Associate certification. ,

title: Introduction to Data Analytics
description: Analytics is at the heart of modern businesses. Data analysts are those professionals which possess the skills and knowledge needed to perform this vital work. This course prepares students for this type of work and for the vendor-neutral CompTIA Data+ (DA0-001) certification. This course is not restricted to those in the Information Technology (IT) field. The skills and knowledge learned along with the CompTIA Data+ certification can be used in any business environment; Healthcare, Business, Data Security and Privacy, and any other consumer area where data is collected and used. ,

title: Introduction to ASP. NET
description:
Students create interactive and dynamic database-driven Web applications using ASP. NET, C# and the .NET Framework. This class is intended for students with fundamental skills in computer programming, HTML, and SQL. Students are strongly encouraged to contact faculty before enrolling in this class to review the prerequisite skills and knowledge needed for successful experience. Prerequisite: CIS 142 , CIS 155 , and CIS 210 , all with a 2.0 or higher, or instructor permission.
,

title: Information System Security I
description: In this course, we will take an in-depth look at information systems security concepts and techniques. We will examine theoretical concepts that make the world of IS security unique. Also, this course will adopt a practical, hands-on approach when examining information systems security techniques. Along with examining different strategies for mitigating security threats, this course will explore the advancement of information assurance as well as timeless problem-solving strategies.
prerequisites: CIS 110 or concurrent enrollment or permission of instructor.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
description: Students learn how to apply behavioral analytics to networks and devices to prevent, detect and combat cybersecurity threats through continuous security monitoring and IT regulatory compliance. Helps prepare students for the CompTIA CySA+ certification. , 2 hours Guided Practice

title: Applications Server Support
description: Introduces the skills necessary to be a server administrator. Concepts covered include server architecture, administration, storage, security, networking, troubleshooting, and disaster recovery. This course helps prepare students for the CompTIA Server+ SK0-004 certification exam. ,

title: Java III
description:
Review the details of the Java language as covered in the Java Certification Oracle Certified Associate Exam 1Z0-808 and Java Certification Oracle Certified Professional Exam 1Z0-809. Topics covered include Core Java APIs, Class Design, Exceptions, Generics, Lambdas, Streams, I/O, Concurrency. Prepares students for the Oracle Certification Exams 1Z0-808 and 1Z0-809. Students are required to take and pass one of the two exams. Prerequisite: CIS 143 OR CS 143 with grade of 2.0 or better, or Instructor Permission.
,

title: Pen Testing

title: Computer Hacking Forensic Investigator
description:
Students learn to use current computer forensic procedures and tools. Students will learn the techniques and processes for detecting cybercrime intrusions, implement the steps to properly extract and evaluate evidence, and conduct system audits to prevent future cybercrimes. Prerequisite: CIS 111 and CIS 182 with a 2.0 or higher, or instructor permission.
,

title: Clinical ​Dental Hygiene II​
description: ​​​​Students apply knowledge of assessment, planning, diagnosis, implementation, evaluation and documentation while providing dental hygiene preventive and therapeutic services to patients in a clinical environment. Patient care includes oral assessment, oral prophylaxis and periodontal maintenance, fluoride treatment, and oral hygiene education.​
prerequisites: Acceptance into and continued enrollment in the dental hygiene program

title: Clinical ​Dental Hygiene III​
description: Students apply knowledge of assessment, planning, diagnosis, implementation, and documentation while providing dental hygiene preventive and therapeutic services to patients in a clinical environment. prerequisites: Acceptance into and continued enrollment in the dental hygiene program

title: Clinical ​Dental Hygiene IV​
description: Continued clinical activities with increased difficulty in the type and number of cases. Students will continue to build confidence in assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, evaluation, and documentation.
prerequisites: Acceptance into and continued enrollment in the dental hygiene program

title: Clinical ​Dental Hygiene V​
description: ​​Continues clinical activities to include treating moderate periodontal patients and patients with moderate/heavy deposits; activities will correlate to theory lecture course. Students will begin to rotate through assigned community externship sites. ​
prerequisites: Acceptance into and continued enrollment in the dental hygiene program

title: Clinical ​Dental Hygiene VI​
description: Continues clinical activities including treatment of patients having moderate to severe periodontal disease with varying levels of calculus. Students will also begin clinical activities that will help prepare them for boards and private practice. ​
prerequisites: Acceptance into and continued enrollment in the dental hygiene program

title: Clinical ​Dental Hygiene VII​
description: A culmination of all previous clinical courses moving through the dental hygiene process of care. prerequisites: Acceptance into and continued enrollment in the dental hygiene program

prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Patient Care and Soft Skills for Sonographers​
description: This course defines the student sonographer's role on the medical team and will prepare learners with basic interpersonal and communication skills needed by medical professionals in the healthcare setting. These skills include effective communication, empathy, dealing with pressure and stress, a strong work ethic, positive mental attitude, adaptability and flexibility, time management, self-confidence, and dealing with criticism constructively. The course emphasizes professionalism in patient care and clinical assessment, as well as interacting with cultural, age, and special needs populations.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway.

title: ​​Sonography Technique Lab I​
description: Hands-on introduction to scanning, knobology, anatomical recognition and image acquisition
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway.

title: ​​Sonography Techniques Lab II​
description: ​Continuation of DMS 102- Sonography techniques lab 1. Hands-on lab course to further develop students scanning skills, knobology, anatomy recognition, image acquisition and proper scanning ergonomics.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway, Successful completion of sonography lab 1 (DMS 102)

title: ​​Sonography Techniques Lab III​
description: Continuation of DMS 103- Sonography techniques lab 2. Hands-on lab course to further develop students' scanning skills, knobology, anatomy recognition, image acquisition, and proper scanning ergonomics.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway, Successful completion of sonography lab 2 (DMS 103)

title: Abdominal Sonography I
description: ​​This course provides an in-depth study of abdominal sonography, focusing on anatomy and sonographic techniques related to abdominal organs. Students will learn to perform and interpret ultrasound examinations of the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, kidneys, spleen aorta and other structures within the abdominal cavity. Emphasis is placed on developing proficiency in scanning techniques, recognizing normal and abnormal sonographic patterns, and understanding the clinical implications of findings.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Cross Sectional Anatomy​
description: ​​Sectional anatomy of the male and female body. Includes anatomical relationships of organs, vascular structures, and body planes and quadrants​.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Small parts and superficial structures​
description: ​​In-depth study of the anatomy and physiology of small parts- thyroid, breast, testicles, and superficial structures such as lymph nodes and soft tissues. This course is designed to include anatomy development, normal and abnormal sonographic appearance, pathophysiology, clinical signs and symptoms, scanning protocols, clinical application, interpretation and reporting.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Abdominal Sonography II​
description: This course is a foundational knowledge progression of abdominal sonography 1 (DMS 110) Focusing and expanding the foundational knowledge gained, more complex and detailed aspects of abdominal anatomy and ultrasound imaging. It covers advanced scanning techniques, interpretation of sonographic images, and the pathophysiology of abdominal organs.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway, successful completion of DMS 110- Abdominal Sonography

title: ​​Ultrasound Physics and Instrumentation I​
description: ​​This course provides an in-depth study of the physical principles and technological concepts in medical ultrasound imaging. Emphasis is placed on understanding the fundamental physics to optimize image quality and ensure patient safety.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Ultrasound Physics and Instrumentation II​
description: ​​This course provides an in-depth study of the physical principles and technological concepts in medical ultrasound imaging. Emphasis is placed on understanding the fundamental physics and emerging techniques to optimize image quality and ensure patient safety.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Successful completion of DMS 120

title: ​​Gyn Sonography and Early Obstetrics​
description: ​​Comprehensive course designed to gain knowledge and ultrasound technology skills in women's health. Emphasis on understanding normal anatomy, pathology, scanning techniques, image interpretation and managing gynecological and early obstetric conditions.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: OB Sonography I
description: This course is a continuation of DMS 130 and focuses on the embryology and sonographic appearances of the fetus and structures of the pregnant uterus during the second and third trimesters. Differentiation of the normal sonographic findings of the fetus and pregnant uterus and measurement parameters are examined. Ethical considerations that may arise during the second and third-trimester gestations will be discussed.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Successful completion of DMS 130

title: Vascular Sonography
description: ​​Vascular terminology, principles including doppler physics. Interpretation of frequency spectral analysis. Intracranial, cerebrovascular and peripheral venous applications related to vascular technology. Normal, abnormal and pathologic states of the human vascular system.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Successful completion of DMS 100, 110, 112 and 116

title: Vascular Sonography Lab
description: ​​This laboratory course provides laboratory experiences that apply to the topics and concepts covered in vascular sonography. Students will build on previous ultrasound knobology knowledge pertaining to vascular scanning and produce vascular sonograms.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Successful completion of DMS 100, 110, 112 and 116. Corequisite: DMS 140

title: ​​Clinical Preparation​
description: ​​Presentation of key concepts related to Diagnostic Medical Sonography Clinical education and required in-services. Focus is on patient care and interpersonal scenarios the externship student will likely face while in the clinical environment. Review and discussion of the DMS Clinical Handbook. Observation required to assigned clinical site in preparation for ​DMS 235- Clinical Education I.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​OB Sonography II​
description: ​​In-depth exploration of abnormal conditions and pathophysiological processes encountered in high-risk obstetrics. This course integrates theoretical knowledge with practical applications to improve clinical competence.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway. Successful completion of DMS 130- GYN sonography and early obstetrics, and DMS 131- OB Sonography I

title: ​​Seminar in Physics​
description: The continuation of ultrasound physics and instrumentation is a new development with advanced analysis of current sonographic practice. Preparation for completion of national registry examination. Students are required to attempt the ARDMS Ultrasound Physics SPI examination.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Clinical Education​ I
description: ​​Clinical preceptorship to introduce students to the fundamental principles and practical applications of diagnostic ultrasound in a clinical setting. This course provides a foundation in ultrasound technology, patient care, and the interpretation of ultrasound images.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Sonographic Subspecialties​
description: This course covers the anatomy and physiology of the neonatal spine, head, Pediatric hip, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal systems. Assessment includes physical and clinical symptoms, laboratory findings, and pathology, including sonographic appearances and patient case studies.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway.

title: Clinical Education II
description: ​​This course provides hands-on experience in the hospital and clinical environment. Emphasis is placed on developing clinical techniques using current ultrasound instrumentation to evaluate pathology. Students then apply the principles of medical, legal, and professional ethics to the patient, physicians, and other members of the health team. ​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway. Prerequisite DMS 235

title: ​​Sonographic Analysis I ​
description: ​Interpretation and critique of normal and abnormal anatomy with correlation of didactic, clinical and image information. Written and oral case presentations with emphasis on gynecological and abdominal subjects.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in DMS pathway.

title: ​​Sonographic Analysis II​
description: Sonographic Analysis enhances critical thinking by teaching students to integrate technological concepts of diagnostic medical sonography into clinical practice. Based on a critical thinking model for student sonographers, this course focuses on interpreting and critiquing normal and abnormal anatomy, correlating didactic, clinical, and image information. It emphasizes communication skills through written and oral case presentations and critiques in general sonography applications. Students also learn the writing process, techniques, formatting, and research for their final project/Capstone presentation. Additional materials cover case studies, abstracts, and peer-reviewed manuscripts. Students are encouraged to publish their final analysis in a peer-reviewed journal or participate in the SDMS Student Poster Competition.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Prerequisite: DMS 250

title: ​​Clinical Education III​
description: ​​Final clinical course. Preceptorship in a medical setting allows students to obtain technical expertise, emphasizing the advanced graduate mastery of knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform all types of sonographic studies and procedures. Emphasis on acquiring competencies at intermediate to advanced level.​
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Prerequisites: DMS 245

title: ​​Sonography Seminar​
description: This course is the cumulative preparation for the ARDMS credentialing board examinations in abdominal sonography and OB/GYN sonography. Review of anatomy, physiology, patient care, clinical signs and symptoms, correlation with other diagnostic testing, and sonographic presentation of normal and abnormal variants and pathologies. Students will participate in discussions utilizing critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and mock examinations. To ensure comprehension of key components students must successfully pass the ARDMS Ultrasound Physics SPI examination by the end of this quarter.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Prerequisite: DMS 110, 115, 116, 130,140 and 213. Co-requisite: DMS 260

title: ​​Clinical Education IV​
description: Final clinical course. Preceptorship in a medical setting allows students to obtain technical expertise, emphasizing the advanced graduate mastery of knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform all types of sonographic studies and procedures. Major emphasis is on terminal competencies leading to program completion.
prerequisites: Continued enrollment in the DMS pathway. Prerequisites: DMS 255

Addresses the application of unmanned aerial vehicles and their sub-systems including maintenance and inspection procedures, basic repair including propellors, cameras, stands, and support equipment. At the completion of the class, the student will be prepared to take the required knowledge test to operate a small UAV in a safe, legal, and within the regulatory requirements. 4 hrs Lecture, 2 hrs Lab

Students will gain an increased understanding of the marginalization of differently abled students and the ramifications of institutionalized academic discrimination. In addition, the course focuses on the various types of exceptionalities including learning challenged students, gifted students, second language learners, the characteristics of such learners, the legal requirements and laws connected to special education, the teacher's role in accommodating the needs of exceptional learners, the role of the family in an exceptional learner's education, inclusive education,and instructional best practices including Universal Design for Learning (UDL), Response to Intervention (RTI), differentiated instruction, among others. title: Reading & Writing in Life & College
description: This intro course helps students develop strategies for reading, writing, reflection, and problem solving. Assignments focus on individual and group processes for personal/academic writing.
prerequisites: Assessment test score or instructor permission.

title: Reading/Writing Academic Disciplines
description:
This course develops students' critical strategies for reading, writing, problem solving, and handling academic life. As an acceleration class with additional lab time, ENGL 099 offers students the opportunity to earn both ENGL 099 and ENGL& 101 credit in one quarter. Prerequisite: Assessment test score, or ENGL 091 with grade of 2.00 or better, or ENGL 092 with grade of 2.00 or better, or instructor permission.

title: Literature of Comic Books and Graphic Novels
description: (H/DSJ) A survey of the rhetoric used in graphic novels and comic books with an emphasis on its representations of social issues and their place in history. The texts will include multiple authors who use comics as a medium to tell powerful stories, some of which are a very personal retelling of their own history. We will be look at the superhero genre as it is the dominant narrative used in comic books/graphic novels but will move beyond this genre towards texts that use this medium to provide powerful narratives and ideologies.

title: The Short Story
description: Humanities The nature and development of short fiction.

title: Introduction to African American Literature
description: (H/DSJ) What is the Black literary tradition, and how does it represent the African/Black American experience? This course surveys African American literature with particular attention to historical and contemporary social contexts. Emphasis is placed on literature and perspectives from a wide spectrum of African American and Black authors, leaders, artists, and activists. Texts may include fiction, poetry, nonfiction, music from hymns to hip hop, cultural artifacts from quilts to fashion, food culture, and other forms of storytelling.

title: Diversity in Contemporary Literature
description: (H/DSJ) Through textual and cultural analysis, this course will cover the different ways in which Contemporary Literature, post 1950, represents struggles for social justice. This course explores how some Contemporary Literature depicts resistance against ideological norms. Contemporary Literature aims to understand how diverse authors negotiate power and privilege through personal, local, and/or global literary works. Texts may include novels, short stories, poetry, drama, graphic novels, social media, and pop culture.

title: Special Topics in Literature
description: Humanities An in-depth study of a single author's work or of selected works by two or more authors related by theme, time period or cultural milieu. This course may be repeated for up to 15 credits.

title: Fantasy Literature
description: Humanities/DSJ From epic hero quests to magical worlds, fantasy represents the power of the imagination. Fantasy's appeal resides in more than just its whimsical fairies, daring protagonists, and frightening monsters; it offers tools for coping with reality and a way to reimagine society. In this class, students will develop close reading and literary analysis skills while exploring how this enduring genre reflects and influences changing ideas about identity, the human condition, utopian dreams, and more. By confronting, reflecting, and subverting our deepest fears and desires, fantasy imagines alternative ways to live.

title: Introduction to Creative Writing
description: Humanities This course focuses on entry-level creative writing practices. We will study introductory craft elements of three genres, including short fiction and poetry. The course will use a workshop model to draft, share, and revise texts. Prerequisite: ENGL 099 with grade of 2.0 or better, or any College Level English Course.

title: Children's Literature
description: (H) This course explores the genres, authors, and illustrators of literature for children from birth through age eight. Methods and criteria for evaluation and curriculum use are also explored. Formerly ECED 178

title: Independent Study
description: Allows the student to pursue topics not offered in the College Catalog through in-depth coursework under the direction of an instructor. This course may include directed readings, coverage of special topics, and other independent study. The topic and scope of study, learning objectives, work required, methods of evaluation, and academic level (195 versus 295) will be determined in conference between the student and instructor. (can be offered in all subjects)
prerequisites: Instructor permission.

title: Science Fiction Literature
description: (H/DSJ) A survey of the literature of science fiction, with an emphasis on the theme of diversity, including the representation of gender, race, social class, sexuality, and culture in the 20th and 21st centuries, as well as the role of diversity in the authorship of science fiction short stories and novels. Authors and works will vary, but may include Shelley, Wells, Bradbury, Asimov, Le Guin, Delaney, Atwood, Butler, and Okorafor. Prerequisite: ENGL& 101 with Grade of 2.0 or better OR ENGL& 111 with grade of 2.0 or better OR AEGS 101 with grade of 2.0 or better.

title: Asian American Literature
description: (H/DSJ) This course surveys Asian American and Pacific Islander American literature from the mid-20th century to the present, with particular attention to the stylistic elements, thematic concerns, and contexts from which the works emerge. Key questions will be asked. With its definitions and boundaries always changing, what exactly does "Asian American literature" or "Pacific Islander American literature" mean? How do histories of war, empire, and colonialism influence such literature? What insights can be learned about Asian American and Pacific Islander empowerment, community formation, and the intersections between race, gender, sexuality, and other forms of social difference? Texts may include novels, short stories, manifestos, drama, manga, poetry, social media, newspapers, protest art, film, food, and pop culture.

title: Native American Literature
description: (H/DSJ) A survey of a wide spectrum of Native American verbal art, from traditional narratives and song to contemporary poetry, fiction, and film. Emphasis on cultural contexts and continuity.

title: British Literature: 19th Century
description: Humanities A survey of Romantic and Victorian British Literature, covering the approximate years 1800 to 1900. Authors and works vary, but may include Wordsworth, Coleridge, Shelley, Keats, Austen, Brontë, Tennyson, Eliot, Browning, Dickens, Thackeray, and Wilde. Prerequisite: ENGL& 101 with grade of 2.0 or better OR ENGL& 111 with grade of 2.0 or better.

title: British Literature: 20th and 21st-Century
description: Humanities A survey of modernism, postmodernism, and postcolonialism in British Literature from 1900 to the present day. Authors and works vary, but may include Conrad, Joyce, Woolf, Auden, Achebe, Rhys, Ballard, Smith, and Rushdie. Prerequisite: ENGL& 101 with grade of 2.0 or better OR ENGL& 111 with grade of 2.0 or better.

title: Creative Writing: Creative Nonfiction
description: Humanities Introduction to the reading, writing, and revising of creative nonfiction. Literary terms and techniques will be presented and applied to original student work and constructive review of original work will provide practical application. This course will include significant critical reading of professional works in the genre. Prerequisite: ENGL& 101 with a grade of 2.0 or better, or ENGL 170 with a grade of 2.0 or better, or instructor permission.

title: Creative Writing: Poetry
description: (H) Introduction to the reading, writing, and revising of poetry. Poetry terms and techniques will be presented and applied to original student work and constructive review of original work will provide practical application. This course will include significant critical reading of professional works in the genre.
prerequisites: ENGL& 101 with a 2.0 or better or ENGL 170 with a 2.0 or better, or Instructor Permission.

title: Creative Writing: Drama
description: Humanities Invention and development of dramatic material: Dialogue, action, stage location, and music. Students and instructor read and critique materials in a workshop setting.

title: Creative Writing: Fiction
description: (H) Introduction to the reading, writing, and revising of fiction. Fiction terms and techniques will be presented and applied to original student work, and constructive review of original work will provide practical application. This course will include significant critical reading of professional works in the genre.
prerequisites: ENGL& 101 with a 2.0 or better or ENGL 170 with a 2.0 or better, or Instructor Permission.

title: Women's Literature
description: Humanities A study of the distinctive contributions of women to literature.

title: Writing in the Disciplines
description: Theory and practice of writing in various academic disciplines. Prerequisite: Successful completion of ENGL& 102 or ENGL& 235 with a minimum GPA of 2.0.

title: Literature and Medicine
description: Humanities A study of medical themes in literature, exploring Different representations of health, illness, and medical practice in novels, short fiction, and poetry. Literature and Medicine places emphasis on the historical and cultural contexts of both the literary works and their medical subjects, as well as how the methods of literary studies contribute to knowledge in the field of medicine. Authors, time periods, and nations covered may vary, but will typically include texts from the 19th and 20th centuries in Britain and America. Prerequisite: Students must be accepted into a bachelor's program at Olympic College or have instructor permission. ENGL& 101 or the equivalent with a 2.0 or better.

title: Composition II
description: A continuation of ENGL& 101 with emphasis on argumentation, research, and documentation. Formerly ENGL 102 Prerequisite: Successful completion of ENGL& 101 with a 2.0 or better or its equivalent.

title: Intro to Literature
description: Humanities A study of major literary forms and methods of interpretation. Formerly ENGL 140

title: Introduction to Fiction: Studies in Literature
description: (H/DSJ) Introduction to methods for close reading and interpreting fiction which may include short stories, novellas, and/or novels. Introduction to diverse authors and how the fictional works are represented, understood, and/or influenced by social, cultural, and historical contexts. Application of social justice and/or diversity theories to fictional texts such as intersectionality, race theory, queer theory, feminist theory, etc.).

title: Intro to Poetry
description: Humanities The course covers a selection of poets writing in English. The nature and development of their poetry and its distinguishing features. Also considers several schools of literary criticism. Formerly ENGL 143 Prerequisite: ENGL& 101 .

title: Intro to Shakespeare
description: Humanities Studies in several major dramas and sonnets. Formerly ENGL 269

title: British Literature I
description: Humanities A survey of the development of English Literature from its beginnings through the later middle ages. Formerly ENGL 266

title: British Literature II
description: Humanities Historically, Renaissance through Enlightenment England saw cultural and technological evolution, religious and political revolution, and colonial expansion amidst international tensions. Beginning with the rediscovery of classical texts, the Renaissance ushered in humanism and its emphasis on reason and agency, ideas developed throughout the Enlightenment inspiring revolution. This course explores Europe's plunge towards modernity through many of England's writers (such as Marlowe, Shakespeare, Donne, Milton, Behn, Finch, Swift, Leapor, Burney, Equiano, Sancho, etc. who contributed literature during this time span). Engl&227 addresses the spark of change in their works, shifting away from Christian themes and writing in the vernacular, demarking what it meant to be British. Formerly ENGL 267 .

title: Technical Writing
description: Problem-solving strategies, information literacy, and research for professional and technical writing settings. Prerequisite: Successful completion of ENGL& 101 with a 2.0 or better or its equivalent.

title: American Literature I
description: Humanities, DSJ Colonization, revolution, expansion, war–early America (1600-1865) was a dynamic period filled with exciting new ideas about individual rights and democratic ideals. But what did this new nation think of itself and its promises? This course explores the establishment of an American identity through its literature. We will examine these narratives in the context of their historical periods, their literary movements, their analysis of culture, and their throughlines to today. Formerly ENGL 260
prerequisites: English&101 as a pre-requisite OR co-requisite

title: American Literature II
description: (H/DSJ) After the Civil War, the push and pull of events and beliefs continued to shape America: Reconstruction and Redemption, immigration and migration, industrialization and war, the American Dream and consumer culture. The tension between tradition and modernization permeated 20th and 21st century America. But what did those traditions represent and what does change mean? English&245 is a literary journey through the American landscapes as a variety of authors examine American culture through various literary movements, genres, and lenses. Formerly ENGL 261
prerequisites: English&101 as a pre-requisite OR a co-requisite.

title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: (NS) Ecological principles, including the interdisciplinary studies of the physical, biological, chemical, and geological principles to understand ecosystems. Focuses on the relationships and connections between humans and their environment, and solutions to environmental problems. Recommended for non-science majors. Community service requirement (12 hours). ,

title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
description: An in-depth look at the structure and the interrelationships between the consumer and the primary, secondary, and auxiliary market segments within the fashion industry.

title: Visual Merchandising & Promotion
description: A comprehensive study of merchandising which includes: presentation, analysis, experimentation and research of the merchandise presentation environment. Learn the practical application of store image, color, texture and display theories of visual merchandising techniques in the fashion industry. Field trips included. ,

title: History of Fashion
description: An overview of costume history in Western culture from ancient civilizations to the present. Examine cultural, social, and historical events and analyze their effect on the history of costume and apparel, including the influence of historical costume on fashion today.

title: Fashion Styling
description: An overview on the art of styling and how to master it. Gain a unique insight as to what it takes creatively to become a fashion stylist by: understanding how to dress Different body types; identify marketing strategies from a styling perspective; and by developing a final project incorporating style, image and identity using visual and written presentation. ,

title: Store Operations
description: Learn the steps needed to develop a retail operation, how to analyze business situations and apply solutions based on sound management theory, and how to examine the processes involved in maintaining a successful retail establishment. ,

title: Fashion Trends and Forecasting
description: Students will develop an understanding of the process, methods and influence of trend analysis and forecasting for the fashion business used for developing a merchandising plan for a retail business.
prerequisites: None.

title: Event Planning
description: Event planning offers the opportunity to develop and present an idea, product or brand from the original idea, through the public relations process, in order to engage with consumers in new and exciting ways. The final project is the actual event.
prerequisites: None.

title: Merchandising in Fashion Capitols
description: Students, under faculty supervision, visit a major fashion capitol to study the factors involved in fashion marketing, design and the international customer's attitudes about fashion. Career opportunities research is included. ,

This course may include directed readings, coverage of special topics, and other independent study. The topic and scope of study, learning objectives, work required, methods of evaluation, and academic level (195 versus 295) will be determined in conference between the student and instructor. (can be offered in all subjects)
prerequisites: Instructor permission.

The topic and scope of study, learning objectives, work required, methods of evaluation, and academic level (195 versus 295) will be determined in conference between the student and instructor. (can be offered in all subjects)
